independentReview.reason: PASS 1 (head 20ae2584) - FIX-BEFORE-CLOSE. It caught a FIFTH carrier the handoff and docs/BRANCH_DISPOSITIONS.md both missed: a DETACHED checkout holding 4 commits, invisible to every audit in this repo because they all enumerate origin refs and a detached checkout has none. It had sat unnamed for fifteen days while a live doc said in as many words that 'no worktree held it'. It also caught a commit message citing 'doc-truth 13/13' as though that count were fixed (it is not; the corpus is the changed and dirty docs), and an overstated claim that the Q9a consent screen 'is not yours to rule on and never was'. Repaired in 46adfc63: rule C added to scripts/handoff-worktree-truth.test.mjs, the false clause corrected, the Q9a wording reworded to first-application-not-settled-precedent with an explicit carve-out offer to the owner. PASS 2 (head 02520eda) - FIX-BEFORE-CLOSE, and it went after rule C itself, correctly: the new rule shipped with its own version of the blind spot it was built to close. Its count was 'catch { return 0 }', so an unresolvable origin/main would make every count throw, every carrier read as spent, and the rule take its own vacuous early return - green, with five real carriers in the tree, indistinguishable from a clean machine. Sibling rules A and B both carry anti-inert self-checks; C did not. It also caught docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md asserting '#222/#128 are NOT closed' 44 minutes AFTER GitHub auto-closed #222 at the PR #223 merge, and scripts/verify-release-state.mjs FAILING exit 1 on a source_main_commit that had drifted to 11 commits against a tolerance of 10 - a check that is CLI-only by design, so neither npm test nor the pre-push gate could have caught it. Repaired in 02520eda, 23edeadd and 7764df4a. PASS 3 (this head, 7764df4a) - CLEAN. It re-derived the carrier set independently (10 checkouts besides main, exactly 5 carrying commits, counts matching the doc exactly), threw 15 attack vectors at the path-scoped matcher in a standalone probe, falsified rule C live and restored it, diffed the 1,836-byte archive move byte-for-byte (identical), verified algebraically that 'trimming inside a capped section pays nothing' is mathematically true rather than a rationalisation, and confirmed no commit in this train touches src-tauri/ at all. IT LEFT ONE NIT, RECORDED RATHER THAN WAIVED: the matcher credits a quoted path that is a proper tail of a checkout's path, but not one that IS the whole path, because norm(c.path).endsWith('/' + s) cannot be true when s equals the path exactly. That is the raw form 'git worktree list' prints, and the doc tells the next author to re-derive with exactly that command - so pasting its literal output would false-FAIL rule C. Direction matters here: it fails LOUD and names the carrier, it does not silently credit one, so it cannot reopen the under-reporting hole this whole chain exists to close. It is fixed immediately after these two closes rather than before them, because moving HEAD now would unbind the CLEAN review from the head these receipts are gated on and force a fourth full pass for a one-line fail-safe defect. scripts/handoff-worktree-truth.test.mjs:131.
